title: 35 MINUTES MOST VIOLENT MORNING PRAYER TO COMMAND THE NEW WEEK
text: Take out your phone right now. Hold it up. I said hold it up. Lift it above your head. That device in your hand is not just a phone. It is a prophetic instrument. It is a delivery system. It is the modern equivalent of the messenger who ran from the battlefield to bring news of victory. In Bible days, they sent runners, they sent horsemen, they sent pigeons. Today, God uses phones. He uses notifications. He uses text messages. He uses emails that land in your inbox at the exact moment you need them. He uses WhatsApp messages that make your heart skip. He uses phone calls that change the direction of your life in 60 seconds. And the spirit of God told me something this morning that made the hair on my arm stand up. He said, "Tell my people to hold their phones up because I am about to sanctify those devices as instruments of good news today. Not eventually, not soon. Today, someone's phone is going to ring, vibrate, ping, or flash with a notification that carries the answer to a prayer they have been praying for months, maybe years. The good news is that close. It is one phone call away, one message away, one notification away. Now, keep that phone in the air for one more moment. And while it is lifted, I want you to do something with your other hand. Open this broadcast and share it. Use that same phone, that prophetic instrument, and share this message with every contact, every group, every platform you have. Because here is the thing, the phone that carries your good news might first need to carry good news to someone else. The blessing follows the distribution. The miracle chases the one who shares. Send this to that friend who has been waiting for a call back on a job. Send it to that sister who has been waiting for test results from the hospital. Send it to that brother who has been waiting for an approval on his visa. Send it to that mother who has been waiting for news about her child. Your phone becomes a miracle conduit when you use it to distribute the word of God. Share it now. Then bring your hands together. We are going into worship. But first lower your phone. But do not put it on silent. Leave it on. I know that sounds strange. In every other service, we tell you to silence your phones. But not today. Today, your phone is part of the service. Today, your phone is on the altar. And before this service ends, God might use that very phone to deliver the evidence that he heard your prayer. Now, worship. Let your voice rise. What a beautiful name it is. What a beautiful name it is. The name of Jesus Christ, my king. What a beautiful name it is. Nothing compares to this. What a beautiful name it is in the name of Jesus. The name of Jesus. The name that Saul heard on the road to Damascus and was changed forever. Acts chapter 9. The name that the crippled man heard at the beautiful gate and leaped to his feet. Acts chapter 3. The name that demons hear and tremble. James 2:1 19. The name that sickness hears and obeys. The name that death hears and releases its grip. The name that poverty hears and flees. That name Jesus. What a beautiful name it is. What a beautiful name it is. In the name of Jesus Christ, my king. You did not deserve the things he has done. No, you did not deserve the things he has done, but he did them anyway. He did them anyway. Yes, Lord. You did them anyway. When we did not deserve mercy, you gave it anyway. When we did not deserve grace, you extended it anyway. When we did not deserve another chance, you provided it anyway. And today, even today, when we may feel unworthy of good news, you are sending it anyway because that is who you are. You are the God of any way. The God who blesses anyway. The God who provides any way. The God who heals any way. The God who promotes anyway. Regardless of what we have done, regardless of where we have been, regardless of how many times we have failed, you show up anyway. One more time. Let it build. What a beautiful name it is in the name of Jesus. Death could not hold you. The veil tore before you. You silence the boast of sin and grave and the heavens are roaring. The praise of your glory for you are raised to life again. He is alive. The one we are praying to this morning is not a dead prophet. [music] He is not a historical figure. He's not a philosophical concept. He is a living God. A breathing, moving, acting, intervening God who is alive right now. And because he's alive, he can hear your prayer. He can see your situation. He can touch your phone. He can arrange your notification. He can orchestrate your phone call. He's alive and he's active in your affairs. Hallelujah. Hallelujah. Hallelujah. Now, let worship shift gently. Let it settle like due. Spirit, lead me where my trust is without borders. Let me walk upon the waters wherever you would call me to take me deeper than my feet could ever wander and my faith will be made stronger in the presence of my savior spirit lead me that is the prayer not lead me to where I am comfortable lead me to where my trust is without borders lead me to the place where my faith has to stretch lead me to the notification I'm afraid to check. Lead me to the phone call I'm scared to answer. Lead me to the message I'm nervous to open. Because on the other side of my fear is my miracle. On the other side of my trembling hand is my good news. On the other side of my hesitation is my breakthrough. Spirit, lead me. Take me deeper. My faith will be made stronger. Hallelujah. Bring the worship to rest now. Like a river settling into its banks after a flood. The water is still there. The power is still present, but it is calm now. Deep and calm, ready to carry whatever God wants to place upon it. Sit down, focus, tune every frequency of your spirit to the voice of the Holy Ghost. Because what I'm about to share is not information. It is activation. How beautiful upon the mountains are the feet of him that bringeth good tidings, that publisheth peace, that bringeth good tidings of good, that publisheth salvation, that saith unto Zion, thy God reignth, good tidings, good news. That is what this verse is about. The beauty of someone who brings good news. In ancient Israel, before phones and telegrams and emails, news traveled by foot, a messenger would run from the battlefield to the king city carrying the report of what happened. And when the watchman on the wall saw the runner approaching, the first thing he tried to determine was, is this good news or bad news? Is the runner smiling or grieving? Is he waving in triumph or limping in defeat? And Isaiah says, "How beautiful are the feet of the one who brings good tidings, not just any tidings, good tidings, news of victory, news of peace, news of salvation, news that makes you shout, "My God reigns." Today, the messenger is not running on foot. The messenger is running through fiber optic cables, through satellite signals, through cellular networks, through Wi-Fi connections. The feet of the good news bearer are digital. And those digital feet are beautiful because they are carrying good tidings, good news, victory reports, breakthrough announcements, healing confirmations, financial approvals, marital confirmations, academic achievements, immigration clearances, good news, and it is coming to your phone today. Now go with me to one more scripture. 2 Kings 7 9-10. This is the story of the four lepers outside the gate of Samaria during a famine. They were starving. They were dying. They decided to surrender to the enemy camp. But when they arrived, the enemy was gone. God had made the enemy hear the sound of a great army, and they had fled, leaving behind food, gold, silver, and clothes. The lepers found abundance where they expected death. And verse 9 says, "Then they said one to another, we do not well. This day is a day of good tidings and we hold our peace. If we tar till the morning light, some mischief will come upon us.
